==English== {{wp}} [[File:Mesh Analysis Example2 TeX.svg|thumb|A circuit with three labelled meshes (sense 6).]] ===Etymology=== {{dercat|en|gmw-pro|inh=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|mesche}}, from {{inh|en|ang|masc||net}} (perhaps influenced in form by related {{cog|ang|mæscre||mesh, spot}}), from the related {{inh|en|gem-pro|*maskwǭ}}{{attn|en|derived?}} and {{m|gem-pro|*maskrǭ}} respectively, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*mezg-||to knit, twist, plait}}. Akin to {{cog|goh|māsca||mesh}}, {{cog|osx|maska||net}}, {{cog|non|mǫskvi}}, {{m|non|mǫskun||mesh}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/mɛʃ/}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛʃ|s=1}} * {{audio|en|en-us-mesh.ogg|a=US}} ===Noun=== {{wikidata lexeme|L17883}} {{en-noun}} # A [[structure]] [[made]] of connected strands of [[metal]], fiber, or other flexible/ductile material, with evenly spaced openings between them. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|III|ii|passage=a golden '''mesh''' to entrap the hearts of men}} # The [[opening]] or space enclosed by the threads of a [[net]] between [[knot]] and knot, or the threads enclosing such a [[space]]. # The [[engagement]] of the teeth of wheels, or of a wheel and rack. # A measure of [[fineness]] (particle [[size]]) of [[ground]] material. A [[powder]] that passes through a [[sieve]] having 300 [[opening]]s [[per]] linear inch but does not pass 400 openings per linear inch is said to be -300 +400 mesh. # {{lb|en|computer graphics}} A [[polygon mesh]]. # {{lb|en|electronics}} In [[mesh analysis]]: a [[loop]] in an [[electric]] [[circuit]] (to which [[Kirchhoff's voltage law]] can be applied). #: {{hypo|en|essential mesh|supermesh}} # {{lb|en|networking}} A [[network topology]] with each [[device]] connected to multiple other devices in [[lieu]] of a central [[switch]]. [[redundancy|Redundancy]] on a mesh network prevents [[single point of failure|single points of failure]]. ====Synonyms==== * {{sense|space and threads}} {{l|en|lattice}}, {{l|en|network}}, {{l|en|net}}, {{l|en|netting}} ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|enmesh|inmesh|intermesh|meshfree|meshless|meshlet|meshlike|meshness|meshwork|meshy|micromesh|nanomesh|synchromesh|unmesh|weldmesh |biomesh |mesh number |mesh network |mesh stick |navigation mesh |polygonal mesh|wiremesh |navmesh| mesh radio |polymesh |submesh |mesh current|mesh hood}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|structure}} * Arabic: * Belarusian: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * German: * Hungarian: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Korean: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|се́тка|f}}, {{t+|ru|сеть|f}} * Slovak: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Ukrainian: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|opening}} * Catalan: * Danish: * Dutch: * Finnish: * French: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Irish: * Italian: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|пе́тля́|f}}, {{t+|ru|яче́йка|f}} * Spanish: * Swedish: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|engagement of teeth of gears}} * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * French: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|зацепле́ние|n}} * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|measure of fineness}} * Finnish: * Hungarian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-see|computing: polygon mesh|polygon mesh}} ===Verb=== {{wikidata lexeme|L17884}} {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To connect together by interlocking, as gears do. # {{lb|en|intransitive|figurative|by extension}} To fit in; to come together harmoniously. #: {{ux|en|The music '''meshed''' well with the visuals in that film.}} #* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=2012-03-30|author=Joe Levy|title=Rockers at Sea|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/01/travel/rock-cruises-bright-spots-for-the-cruise-and-music-industries.html|passage=The headliners — Weezer and Dinosaur Jr. — were alt rock acts that had turned the sound of disconnection into an audience almost two decades ago. Exactly how that was going to '''mesh''' with blue skies and umbrella drinks wasn’t clear to me.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251102113957/https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/01/travel/rock-cruises-bright-spots-for-the-cruise-and-music-industries.html|archivedate=2 November 2025}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To catch in a mesh. #* {{quote-book|en|year=a. 1547|author=w:Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey|title=Description of the fickle affections, pangs, and slights of love |passage=I know how loue doth rage vpon a yelding minde:
How smal a net may take and '''meash''' a hart of gentle kinde}} ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|meshable|remesh}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|to connect together by interlocking, as gears do}} * Hungarian: * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|fit in, come together}} * French: * German: * Hungarian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|сочетаться|impf}}, {{t+|ru|подходить|impf}} * Serbo-Croatian: {{trans-bottom}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=ehms|Hems|Mehs|Shem|hems|mehs}}
